previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after his tunneled central line spontaneously displaced, interrupting his continuous remodulin infusion for portopulmonary hypertension. He was stabilized with a peripheral IV remodulin infusion and underwent urgent placement of a new right internal jugular tunneled catheter, which was successfully implanted with the tip in the right atrium. He tolerated the procedure well without complications. His chronic conditions, including cirrhosis, ascites, thrombocytopenia, and vertebral compression fractures, remained stable. He resumed his home remodulin dose through the new line and was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor weight, manage his line, and follow up with transplant clinic. No new infections or procedural complications occurred.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Large volume ascites, requiring weekly paracentesis.

TECHNIQUE:  After an explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives,
written informed consent was obtained.  Limited ultrasound of all four
quadrants revealed a large amount of ascites.  A spot was marked in the left
lower quadrant for paracentesis.  A pre-procedure timeout was performed to
verify the patient's identity, using three patient identifiers, as well as the
procedure to be performed.  The spot was prepped and draped in the standard
sterile fashion and 1% lidocaine was used to anesthetize the soft tissues.  A
5 ___ ___ catheter was inserted through the peritoneum and 4 liters of
clear amber ascites was removed.  Samples were sent for cell count,
differential and Gram stain as per orders.  The patient tolerated the
procedure well and there were no immediate complications.  A cutaneous stitch
was placed to the paracentesis site given patient's history of leaking after
paracentesis.  The attending radiologist, Dr. ___, was present and supervised
the procedure.

IMPRESSION:  Successful therapeutic and diagnostic ultrasound-guided
paracentesis yielding 4 liters of ascites.

PARACENTESIS

INDICATION:  Patient with HCV cirrhosis requiring frequent paracentesis
usually 12 liters, now with abdominal distention and pain.  Please remove at
least 8 liters of fluid.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ Dr. ___.

TECHNIQUE:  

The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed with the
patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedure timeout was
performed, discussing the planned procedure, confirming the patient's identity
with three identifiers, reviewing a checklist per ___ protocol.

The patient was positioned supine on the ultrasound table.  Under US guidance
an entrance site was selected in left lower fossa.  The skin was prepped and
draped in usual sterile fashion.  10 cc of lidocaine 1% was instilled for
local anesthesia.  Using a 5 ___ ___ catheter connected to suction, 8
liters of ascites was removed.  There was no complication after the procedure.

IMPRESSION:

Ultrasound-guided therapeutic paracentesis yielding 8 liters of ascites.
